(NYSE: EFOR), today announced it has secured a three-year, sole-source indefinite-delivery/indefinite-quantity (IDIQ) contract expansion with a ceiling of $148 million to continue supporting the Chief Digital and AI Office’s (CDAO) Secure Unclassified Network (SUNet), building on more than a decade of support for the program. Additionally, Everforth ECS was selected under a Commercial Solutions Opening (CSO) to research and prototype the next generation of capabilities for SUNet 2.0, advancing CDAO modernization priorities.
Under the expanded SUNet contract, Everforth ECS will continue to manage and maintain the operational environment while supporting the transition of mission capabilities to future SUNet architecture.

The contract expansion follows Everforth ECS’ selection to prototype SUNet 2.0 on behalf of the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Research and Engineering and the CDAO. SUNet 2.0 is designed to provide Department of War (DoW) organizations and mission partners with a secure digital environment to collaborate and rapidly develop, test, and validate emerging

Together, the awards position Everforth ECS to sustain today’s mission while helping shape the next generation of SUNet capabilities. Everforth ECS brings more than a decade of operational experience supporting SUNet, giving the team a deep understanding of its users, mission requirements, and operating environment as the Government explores the next phase of the platform.

“These awards represent the next chapter of a mission we have supported alongside the Department of War and its mission partners for more than a decade,” said Donnie Scott, president of Everforth ECS. “While we continue to keep SUNet secure and responsive to the mission, we will also help transition to what comes next. By bringing our operational knowledge together with modern cloud, cybersecurity, automation, and AI capabilities, we can provide CDAO and its mission partners a faster, more secure way to experiment, collaborate, and turn emerging technologies into operational capability.”

Everforth ECS supports SUNet across its full lifecycle for the DoW, sustaining the current enterprise for existing mission users while developing SUNet 2.0, a secure sandbox for rapid AI/ML experimentation. The modernization effort will explore modern hybrid cloud, zero trust controls, and modern data management capabilities designed to reduce the time required to onboard users and move new capabilities toward mission use.

“Our many years supporting SUNet have taught us our users’ challenges, what they're constrained by, and what actually moves their mission forward,” said Brian Orsi, CDAO account lead at Everforth ECS. “That experience is shaping every part of this modernization, with the goal of giving mission partners a faster, more secure way to test, integrate, and operationalize emerging capabilities.”

For the DoW, CDAO, and their mission partners, the result is a path to sustain what works today while building a faster, more secure, and more adaptable foundation for DoW AI, data, and mission collaboration in the future.

Everforth ECS, the Federal Government Segment of Everforth, is a trusted mission operations partner helping government agencies deliver measurable outcomes through advanced technology solutions, including AI, cybersecurity, digital engineering, and enterprise modernization. By bringing together deep mission expertise, proven processes, and the right technologies, Everforth ECS helps customers accelerate decision making, strengthen resilience, and modernize the systems that power the government’s most critical missions. For more information, visit www.everforthecs.com.
